risks.note: Competitiveness, costs and profitability depend on the ability to source and maintain a stable, sufficient supply of limestone, gypsum, fly ash, granulated slag, iron ore and laterite at acceptable prices; prices are uncertain due to climatic conditions, commodity price fluctuations, transportation costs and government policy changes.

The Indian cement industry is highly competitive and dominated by a few large pan-India manufacturers; in the southern region the Company faces well-established local competitors on price, quality and brand.

Demand from cement-consuming sectors (infrastructure, housing, commercial real estate) is heavily dependent on continued government infrastructure spending; any pullback in government initiatives could trigger a recession in the cement industry.
risks.risk: Risk of change in Government policies

risks.note: The cement industry is energy intensive and requires continuous power and fuel supply; production costs are adversely impacted by rising power, fuel and freight costs, and any rise in international coal prices would raise operating costs.
The Company relies on road transportation for dispatches; rising diesel prices have increased transportation costs and the heavy dependence on road transport adversely impacts operating costs.
Increased demand is expected to bring intense competition, which may adversely impact the Company's market share, sales volume and profitability.

Operations, including the significantly automated manufacturing process, depend heavily on IT/ERP systems; effective cyber security is required to protect hardware and software from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorized access, modification and disclosure.

Attrition and non-availability of required talent resources can affect overall performance; recruiting, training and retaining talent, and placing the right people in the right roles, are cited as critical challenges.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Competitiveness, costs and profitability depend on the ability to source and maintain a stable, sufficient supply of limestone, gypsum, fly ash, granulated slag, iron ore and laterite at acceptable prices; prices are uncertain due to climatic conditions, commodity price fluctuations, transportation costs and government policy changes.
- The Indian cement industry is highly competitive and dominated by a few large pan-India manufacturers; in the southern region the Company faces well-established local competitors on price, quality and brand.
- Demand from cement-consuming sectors (infrastructure, housing, commercial real estate) is heavily dependent on continued government infrastructure spending; any pullback in government initiatives could trigger a recession in the cement industry.
- The cement industry is energy intensive and requires continuous power and fuel supply; production costs are adversely impacted by rising power, fuel and freight costs, and any rise in international coal prices would raise operating costs.
- The Company relies on road transportation for dispatches; rising diesel prices have increased transportation costs and the heavy dependence on road transport adversely impacts operating costs.
- Increased demand is expected to bring intense competition, which may adversely impact the Company's market share, sales volume and profitability.
- Operations, including the significantly automated manufacturing process, depend heavily on IT/ERP systems; effective cyber security is required to protect hardware and software from misuse, interference, loss, unauthorized access, modification and disclosure.
- Attrition and non-availability of required talent resources can affect overall performance; recruiting, training and retaining talent, and placing the right people in the right roles, are cited as critical challenges.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on core markets — the Company cut down non-core market sales to concentrate on its core markets.
- Selling certain cement products under the Chettinad Brand to its parent company to improve capacity utilisation and sales performance.
- Continuing to improve operational efficiency through kiln optimisation, debottlenecking of equipment, and reducing equipment breakdowns.
- Increasing use of alternative fuel resources to improve cost efficiency and reduce coal usage.
- Improving efficiency of dispatches by increasing bulk cement dispatches to reduce dependence on road transportation.
